# gh-1507: [feat] Activate reviewer pool execution: producers, reviewers config, CI wiring (active half of #1406)

## Description

Implements the **active half** of #1406 (reviewer pool). The library half shipped in gh-1471 / PR #1481 and is currently dormant — nothing in production invokes it. Part of the #1391/#1328 review quality line.

## What already exists (inert half, merged)

- `js/common/reviewPool.js` + `js/common/reviewPoolAggregate.js` — pool execution primitives (candidate leg dispatch, candidates wiring, marker producers, filter merge point).
- Seams: `js/common/mergeGate.js` + `js/common/reviewPolicy.js` already reference the pool (filter merge / required-reviewer merge gate surfaces).
- Skill-file pattern per #1406: factory `instructions/review/<name>.json` + repo `.dmtools/review/<name>.json`, merged by name; schema `name` + `lens` required, everything else defaulted (`rounds: ["all"]`, `isEnabled: true`, `isFiltered: true`, `isRequired: false`, `filterWeight: normal`, `triggerPaths: []`, `mayRaise: ALL`, `options: {}`).
- **Gap**: no producer calls the dispatcher — no SM rule, no root agent config, no workflow reference; and the pool's own unit tests (`test_reviewPoolAggregate.js`, `test_reviewPoolCandidates.js`, `test_reviewPoolPost.js`) are not registered in `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` nor wired into CI, so they never execute anywhere.

## Goal — one sentence

**A configured repository can turn on specialist reviewer legs (base + named specialists) for a PR review round: candidates are dispatched, their findings flow through the filter merge into the normal verdict census, and a `required` reviewer blocks the merge until its lane passes.**

## What ships (scope)

1. **Producers**: the review path dispatches pool candidate legs when `reviewPolicy.reviewers` names enabled reviewers — same trigger surface as today's single review leg (label/SM rule unchanged; the pool rides behind the existing review entry).
2. **Config**: `reviewPolicy.reviewers` (list of `{name, ...overrides}` per the #1406 defaults table) honored from the repo's `.dmtools/config.js`; factory `instructions/review/<name>.json` skill files provide the lens texts; unknown names fail loud at config load, not silently.
3. **Filter merge**: candidate findings → cross-reviewer dedup → weighted retention (`filterWeight`) → dropped-findings surfaced visibly → ONE census feeding the existing gh-1351 verdict (no second verdict layer).
4. **Required gate**: `isRequired: true` reviewers integrate with the gh-1370 merge-time resolution check — head-carried lane PASS markers; retry → escalate on repeated lane failure.
5. **Rounds + triggerPaths**: `rounds` array-of-flags counts completions (first-counts); `triggerPaths` scoping includes/excludes a reviewer by changed-path globs.
6. **Tests registered + CI wiring**: the three dormant pool test files enter `run_all.json` (or an explicitly CI-invoked topic runner) — the silent-skip closes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — a repo config with `reviewers: [{name: security, isRequired: true}]` produces: base review + specialist candidate leg(s), merged dedup'd census, verdict unchanged in shape.
- AC2 — a BLOCKING finding from a `required` specialist holds the merge until resolved (gh-1370 lane clause fires).
- AC3 — a repo WITHOUT `reviewPolicy.reviewers` behaves byte-identically to today (no dispatch, no extra legs, no census change) — negative test.
- AC4 — `triggerPaths` excludes a specialist on non-matching diffs (no leg, no census entry).
- AC5 — the three pool test files execute in CI (registered or topic-runner wired) and pass.
- AC6 — unknown reviewer name in config → loud config-load error (fail-fast, not silent skip).

## Test plan

- Unit: extend the three existing pool suites (dispatch, candidates wiring, marker producers, aggregate/filter merge) + registration coverage (run_all includes them).
- IT: config fixtures through reviewPolicy validation (unknown name → error; defaults table honored).
- REG: single-reviewer-less configs produce identical census/verdict artifacts as before (golden diff).

## Out of scope (per #1406 decisions)

- Legal reviewer as factory default (repo configuration only).
- Majority voting, lessons/feedback loop, polish-lap changes — separate issues.

## References

#1406 (spec + defaults table), #1481 / gh-1471 (inert half), #1403 (filter leg, landed), #1370 (resolution gate), #1351 (verdict layer), gh-1370 lane clause.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
# Grandfathering code that newly ENTERS the gate (a file that was previously
#   uninstrumentable, so all its functions were N/A): merge the PR head's
#   `NEW > threshold` entries into the released asset (max of old/new never
#   needed — they are absent) and `gh release upload --clobber` it before the PR
#   runs; --update-baseline never adds entries by itself.
# Coverage holes fail: the instrument step runs with --exit-on-error and the
#   ratchet step re-runs crap4js with --require-coverage over production js/**.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Duplication gate (gh-1251): a second, independent gate fails PRs and main on
# NEW or GROWING JS duplication. The measurement is
# `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci`; a
# pinned set of production files already exceeds 1% today (pre-existing debt
# owned by the gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets — see duplication-baseline.json
# for the current pinned set), so the gate is a RATCHET against that
# baseline, not an absolute bar — it fails only when a file over threshold is
# not pinned or a pinned file gained ABSOLUTE duplicated lines
# (ci/duplicationRatchet.js; percentage shifts from file shrinkage are
# informational, not failures). Its clones-mode report also feeds the README
# `duplication` endpoint badge published from the same run.
#
# Runtime-artifact guard (gh-1365): two read-only `git ls-files` queries over the
# checked-out INDEX (no working-dir state involved — robust on PR checkouts and
# dirty runner workspaces) hard-fail the job when pipeline-owned runtime artifacts
# are tracked: (1) a tracked file matching the checked-in gitignore-style pattern
# list ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt — extend THAT file, not this workflow; (2)
# a file matching .gitignore but still tracked — the missed-cleanup signature of
# the gh-1358/.dmtools-target-workingdir incident. A modified TRACKED artifact
# blocks every dev-leg checkout; untracked+ignored copies are harmless by
# construction.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '2d99360df25cec4c7e713801eb2f6e7ebc7495fb'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Runtime-artifact guard (tracked artifacts / tracked-but-ignored)
        # gh-1365: pipeline-owned runtime artifacts must never be tracked — a modified
        # TRACKED artifact in a runner workspace blocks every dev-leg checkout (the
        # gh-1358/.dmtools-target-workingdir incident), while an untracked+ignored
        # copy is harmless by construction. Both checks are read-only `git ls-files`
        # queries evaluated against the checked-out INDEX — no working-dir state is
        # consulted, so dirty runner workspaces cannot influence the verdict:
        #  1. tracked files matching ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt — the checked-in
        #     gitignore-style list deployments extend WITHOUT touching this workflow;
        #  2. tracked files matching the repo's own ignore rules (`--exclude-standard`)
        #     — the "tracked but ignored" state, i.e. the missed-cleanup signature.
        # Any hit fails the job naming the file and the exact remediation (never just
        # a count); both checks always run so one bad tree reports every violation.
        run: |
          set -e
          patterns="ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt"
          status=0
          report="$(mktemp)"

          hits="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-from="$patterns")"
          if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "Tracked files match \`$patterns\` — runtime artifacts must never be tracked. Untrack each one:"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\` and add the path to .gitignore"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked runtime artifact matches $patterns — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\" and add the path to .gitignore"
              done <<EOF
          $hits
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked file matches \`$patterns\`."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          ignored="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-standard)"
          if [ -n "$ignored" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "These tracked files match the repo's own .gitignore rules but are still tracked (the missed-cleanup signature — untrack so the ignore rule takes effect):"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\`"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked but matches .gitignore — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\""
              done <<EOF
          $ignored
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked-but-ignored files."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          cat "$report"
          cat "$report" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit $status

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        id: instrument
        # --exit-on-error: a file that fails to instrument (e.g. a duplicate
        # top-level declaration) FAILS the job instead of being copied raw —
        # a raw copy has no coverage, so every function in it would drop out
        # of the CRAP gate unnoticed. Intentionally uninstrumented (copied
        # verbatim below): the harness itself (js/unit-tests/testRunner.js —
        # it redeclares its shared loaders by design) and js/test/**
        # (node:test suites run outside the harness).
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --exit-on-error \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/testRunner.js' --exclude 'js/test/**' \
            --cwd . . "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only instrumented sources — add the
          # json/md/sh/.mjs/.cjs payloads the suite reads (configs,
          # instructions, prompts, fixtures; .mjs/.cjs stay raw as before)…
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # …and the intentionally uninstrumented .js files excluded above.
          rsync -a --ignore-existing --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          # Production functions without a CRAP score (N/A coverage or a parse
          # failure) are invisible to the ratchet above — fail on any of them.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" js \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/**' --exclude 'js/test/**' --exclude 'js/integration-tests/**' \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 \
            --require-coverage > /dev/null || code=2
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Review skill files (lens/contract CI gate)
        # The reviewer pool's skill files are CONTRACT, not prose: every
        # reviewer (factory instructions/review/*.json + repo .dmtools/review/*.json)
        # must resolve to an existing non-empty lens, same-name files may only
        # TUNE factory reviewers, duplicate names are rejected, and the
        # promptAppend / reviewPolicy.reviewers targets must exist. Fails the
        # PR before a misconfigured reviewer silently drops out of the pool.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: node scripts/validate-review-skills.js .

      - name: Module-size ratchet (<= 800 lines / 40 top-level functions per module)
        # Per-function CRAP never flags a god module made of small functions.
        # Production modules (js/**, tests excluded) must stay within 800
        # physical lines and 40 top-level functions; modules already over a
        # limit are pinned in ci/module-size-baseline.json with their current
        # size and may only shrink (crap4js module-size --baseline). After
        # splitting a pinned module, lower its pin (re-run with
        # --write-baseline) so the gain is locked in.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" module-size \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/**' --exclude 'js/test/**' --exclude 'js/integration-tests/**' \
            --baseline ci/module-size-baseline.json js

      - name: Nesting gate (control-flow nesting <= 5)
        # Pre-existing offenders carry a `// ignore:nesting` marker above the
        # function; new deep nesting fails.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: '"$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" nesting js'

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)
        # Dynamic shields.io endpoint badges: the numbers come from this run, the JSON lives on an
        # orphan 'badges' branch, so nothing in the code tree changes (no PR conflicts, no bot
        # commits on main). Cosmetic — never fails the pipeline.
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart/releases/download/v0.15.0/crap4dart-linux-x64 \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64" && chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64" check --only similarity --format json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/md-similarity-check.json" 2>/dev/null || true
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap4dart-linux-x64" similarity --jaccard 0.01 --containment 0.01 --format json > "$RUNNER_TEMP/md-similarity-all.json" 2>/dev/null || true
          # clones-mode report carries the project-wide duplicated-line percentage
          # in its summary line; the gate itself runs (and may fail) earlier.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --report clones --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/duplication.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
          node - <<'JS'
          const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
          const tmp = process.env.RUNNER_TEMP, thr = Number(process.env.CRAP_THRESHOLD);
          const cov = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'cov/coverage-final.json'), 'utf8'));
          let t = 0, h = 0;
          for (const [f, e] of Object.entries(cov)) {
            if (/\/(unit-tests|test)\//.test(f)) continue;       // product code only
            for (const k in e.s) { t++; if (e.s[k] > 0) h++; }
          }
          const report = fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'crap-all.txt'), 'utf8');
          const rows = report.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim().split(/\s+/)).filter((c) => c.length >= 5 && /\.(js|mjs|cjs)$/.test(c[1]) && !/\/(unit-tests|test)\//.test(c[1]) && !isNaN(parseFloat(c[c.length - 1])));
          const scores = rows.map((c) => parseFloat(c[c.length - 1]));
          const max = Math.max(0, ...scores), over = scores.filter((x) => x > thr).length;
          const pct = t ? Math.round((1000 * h) / t) / 10 : 0;
          const colorMax = max <= 12 ? 'brightgreen' : max <= 30 ? 'yellow' : max <= 200 ? 'orange' : 'red';
          const colorOver = over === 0 ? 'brightgreen' : over <= 25 ? 'yellow' : over <= 150 ? 'orange' : 'red';
          const colorCov = pct >= 90 ? 'brightgreen' : pct >= 80 ? 'green' : pct >= 70 ? 'yellowgreen' : pct >= 50 ? 'yellow' : 'orange';
          const out = path.join(tmp, 'badges');
          fs.mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
          const w = (n, label, message, color) => fs.writeFileSync(path.join(out, n), JSON.stringify({ schemaVersion: 1, label, message, color }) + '\n');
          w('crap-max.json', 'CRAP max', String(Math.round(max * 10) / 10), colorMax);
          w('crap-over.json', `CRAP > ${thr}`, `${over} fns`, colorOver);
          w('coverage.json', 'coverage', `${pct}%`, colorCov);
          let mdPairs = 0, maxJaccard = 0;
          try {
            const sim = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'md-similarity-check.json'), 'utf8'));
            const gate = (sim.gates || []).find((g) => g.id === 'similarity') || {};
            mdPairs = Array.isArray(gate.violations) ? gate.violations.length : 0;
          } catch (_) {}
          try {
            const allSim = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'md-similarity-all.json'), 'utf8'));
            const pairs = Array.isArray(allSim.pairs) ? allSim.pairs : [];
            if (pairs.length > 0) maxJaccard = Math.max(0, ...pairs.map((p) => Number(p.jaccard) || 0));
          } catch (_) {}
          const maxPct = Math.round(maxJaccard * 100);
          const mdMsg = mdPairs === 0 ? `max ${maxPct}% (0 over 50%)` : `max ${maxPct}% (${mdPairs} over 50%)`;
          const mdColor = mdPairs > 0 ? 'red' : maxJaccard <= 0.35 ? 'brightgreen' : maxJaccard <= 0.45 ? 'green' : 'yellow';
          w('md-similarity.json', 'md similarity', mdMsg, mdColor);
          let dupPct = null, dupGroups = 0;
          try {
            const dupReport = fs.readFileSync(path.join(tmp, 'duplication.txt'), 'utf8');
            const dupLines = dupReport.split('\n');
            for (const l of dupLines) {
              const m = l.match(/(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)% duplicated lines\s*$/);
              if (m) dupPct = parseFloat(m[1]);
              const g = l.match(/^(\d+) clone groups/);
              if (g) dupGroups = parseInt(g[1], 10);
            }
          } catch (_) {}
          if (dupPct !== null) {
            const dupColor = dupPct < 1.0 ? 'brightgreen' : dupPct < 2.0 ? 'green' : dupPct < 5.0 ? 'yellow' : dupPct < 10.0 ? 'orange' : 'red';
            w('duplication.json', 'duplication', `${dupPct}% (${dupGroups} groups)`, dupColor);
          }
          console.log(`badges: max=${max} over=${over} coverage=${pct}% duplication=${dupPct === null ? 'skipped' : dupPct + '%'}`);
          JS
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/badges"
          git init -q && git checkout -q -b badges
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'; git config user.email 'github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add -A && git commit -q -m "badges: main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          git push -q -f "https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection-String-Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git" badges

      - name: Label PR (crap:regression / crap:improved)
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          OUTCOME: ${{ steps.ratchet.outcome }}
          IMPROVED: ${{ steps.ratchet.outputs.improved }}
        run: |
          if [ "$OUTCOME" = "failure" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:regression || true
          elif [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --remove-label crap:regression || true
          fi
          if [ "$IMPROVED" = "true" ] && [ "$OUTCOME" = "success" ]; then
            gh pr edit "$PR" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --add-label crap:improved || true
          fi

"**Config**: `reviewPolicy.reviewers` (list of `{name, ...overrides}` per the #1406 defaults table) honored from the repo's `.dmtools/config.js`; factory `instructions/review/<name>.json` skill files provide the lens texts; unknown names fail loud at config load, not silently."

And AC6: "unknown reviewer name in config → loud config-load error (fail-fast, not silent skip)".

So the ticket REQUIRES: when config names an unknown reviewer, the leg fails loudly at config load (like gh-1351 policy validation does in loadContext). Currently: the unknown-name error is thrown by resolvePool only when the pool is resolved in the pre-cli/post actions, where both call sites swallow it (non-fatal catch). So AC6 is NOT met end-to-end in the production path — only the unit-level mechanism exists.

How to implement fail-fast at config load cleanly, following the gh-1351 pattern (loadContext hard-validates)? In loadContext after resolveReviewPolicy, we could validate reviewer names against the pool. But loadContext doesn't have io for the pool dirs... Actually it can — file_read/file_list are dmtools globals available at action time. reviewPoolModule.resolvePool(poolResolveIoOf(...), ctx.config, ctx.jp) would resolve everything (warnings too). Hmm, but resolving the pool in loadContext duplicates the pre-cli resolution (which happens later in reviewerPoolRoundSetup). A cleaner approach matching existing conventions: in `reviewerPoolRoundSetup`'s catch, RE-THROW errors that are config errors (ReviewSkillValidationError family — isReviewSkillError), and only swallow operational errors. That's a precise fail-loud: a misconfigured pool fails the leg (with the error comment posted by action()'s catch → postSetupErrorComment), while operational failures stay fail-open.

Wait, but there's a subtlety: resolvePool also throws for `reviewPolicy.required` unknown names, duplicate names, invalid JSON skill files, repo tuning contract violations — ALL genuine config errors of the same family (skillError / ReviewSkillValidationError). All should fail loud per the ticket's doctrine ("the misconfiguration must fail the leg at start, never silently no-op" — that's literally in reviewPool.js applyPolicyTuning's comment!). 

So the fix: in reviewPoolLegSetup.reviewerPoolRoundSetup, distinguish ReviewSkillValidationError (config errors → rethrow, leg fails loudly) from other errors (operational → warn, fail-open). Same for resolvePostingPoolOrNull in postPReviewComments? The post action is after the pre-cli action — if the pre-cli already failed the leg on config errors, the post never runs. But belt-and-braces: the post could also rethrow config errors. Hmm — the post action's failure handling... let me check how postPReviewComments handles action errors. Actually, keep the post side fail-soft? If the pre-cli failed the leg, post never happens. But what if pool resolution succeeds in pre-cli but fails in post (io difference)? Ultra-edge; keep post as-is (fail-open) — no wait, consistency matters. Let me look at what the tests currently assert about the non-fatal catch, and how the post action wraps runPoolRound.

Also for AC1 — the config SHAPE question (list vs map). Decision: the ticket says "list of `{name, ...overrides}` per the #1406 defaults table". The current schema is a map `{name: {tunables}}`. Two options:
(a) Extend validateReviewersTuning to ALSO accept the list shape, normalizing `[{name: 'security', isEnabled: true}]` → `{security: {...}}`. This honors the ticket text directly.
(b) Keep the map shape and declare the ticket's phrasing descriptive of the #1406 spec's defaults table (the shipped schema deliberately evolved; the map + `required` list is the merged gh-1406 revision).

Hmm. The defaults table in the ticket includes `isRequired: false` as a schema default for reviewer entries — the shipped schema has NO isRequired field at all (requiredness is the pool-level `required` list). Supporting `isRequired` per-reviewer would require adding it to the schema/tuning... that's re-opening a closed design decision that the merged half deliberately made differently (the §7 2026-11-12 revision comments). 

Careful. The agent guidelines say: "Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things." The codebase HAS an established way. The ticket's AC1 wording "a repo config with `reviewers: [{name: security, isRequired: true}]`" describes the SPEC's example config; the shipped schema realizes requiredness via `required: ['security']`. The FUNCTIONAL requirement of AC1 is: base review + specialist leg(s) + merged dedup'd census + verdict shape unchanged — which the map shape supports: `reviewPolicy: {reviewers: {security: {isEnabled: true}}, required: ['base','security']}` (or just default required).

Hmm, but honestly, accepting BOTH shapes is more robust and directly satisfies the ticket text. The list shape `[{name, ...}]` — with tunables only (isEnabled/rounds/triggerPaths/options/model) plus... isRequired? If I accept isRequired in the list shape, I'd map it to the required list. That's schema synthesis beyond the established pattern...

Let me look at the #1406 spec if it's fetchable — the ticket references "#1406 (spec + defaults table)". This is a GitHub issues repo (gh- prefix). The repo is github.com/nicku/dmtools-agents? Actually the AGENTS.md references https://github.com/nicku/dmtools. Let me try fetching issue #1406 via dmtools github_get_issue or web. The input folder doesn't have it. The instructions say: "IMPORTANT When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER".

Let me find the repo owner: git remote -v.

#1391 (the analysis + measured problem). Dependencies: **#1403 (filter leg) is a hard prerequisite** — the pool's aggregation point. Related: #1404 (review-prompt decision-rule rewrite — separate, ships independently), https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15134 (ByteDance BitsAI-CR — the generate→filter pattern this implements), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10515-026-00638-5 (why prompt edits must swap the decision rule, not add detail).

## Problem

The review leg is a single generalist: it catches security only in plain sight, and domain depth (consent/privacy/terms, framework idioms) needs dedicated lenses. Meanwhile every rework-tier finding arms a rework lap (15–20 CI min), so precision matters as much as recall. We need **configurable specialist reviewers** that extend a shared base — without forking dmtools-agents, and without breaking the machine contract.

> **Revision 2026-11-12 (owner decision):** the per-reviewer `isRequired` field is REMOVED from the skill-file schema. Merge gating moves to pool policy: `reviewPolicy.required: [names]` — one place, repo-owned ("merge rules are repo rules"). Factory default policy: `['base', 'security']`. All §2/§3/§7/§8/§10 below reflect this.

## The invariants (binding — no interpretation)

1. **One census, one verdict.** Specialists produce CANDIDATES only (structured findings). They never post threads directly, never emit a PR verdict, never approve/request-changes. The filter leg (§5) merges all candidates into one census; gh-1351 machine recomputation stays the only decider.
2. **Extend, never replace.** Repo config can ADD reviewers and APPEND prompt files to factory reviewers. It cannot replace factory lens/contract files, cannot remove factory reviewers from the pool, and cannot re-define factory reviewers' contract fields.
3. **Contract immutability.** The base contract files (output schema, verdict/tier rules, census rules, registry protocol, citation rule) are factory invariants — the machine parses what they mandate (gh-1350/1351/1332).
4. **`first` counts completions, not attempts.** A failed leg (429/timeout) re-fires next round until the reviewer's completion marker exists — budget-bounded, then owner escalation (gh-957 doctrine: budget exhaustion escalates, never approves).
5. **Fail-open vs merge gate are different concerns.** Availability failures are fail-open for non-required reviewers (round proceeds, packet notes it). `reviewPolicy.required` reviewers gate the MERGE (§7) — availability failures there mean retry→escalate, never merge.

## 1. Instructions layout — nested, no new top-level folders

```
instructions/pr_review/
    base/                        ← the reviewer-agnostic CONTRACT (factory)
        input_context.md, output_rules.md, review_verdict_rules.md,
        registry_protocol.md, formatting_rules.md, few_shots_format.md
    generalist/                  ← the base lens (today's general_guidelines §1–§7)
        lens.md, few_shots.md
    security/                    ← the factory security specialist
        lens.md                  ← hunt bullets + reference-pack pointer
        few_shots.md
```

Every reviewer's prompt assembles as `[roleLine → pr_review/base/* → lens → repo append files (if any) → few-shots + verdict rules]` — contract files stay LAST (recency). Renaming the base role line is part of this change: today it claims "Senior Code Reviewer & **Security Expert**" — deep security moves to the specialist.

Ship a CI freshness gate: every reviewer leg's prompt list must include the full `pr_review/base/` set (docs-coverage-gate style). `pr_test_automation_review` migrates to the same base set (today it duplicates it).

## 2. Skill files — a reviewer is a JSON file

Two locations, loaded and MERGED by name:
- factory: `instructions/review/<name>.json` (shipped with dmtools-agents; base + security)
- repo: `.dmtools/review/<name>.json` (repo-defined reviewers; repo can never re-define factory ones' contract — a same-name `security.json` may only TUNE `isEnabled/rounds/triggerPaths/options/model`)

**Base schema — universal fields only; required = `name` + `lens`; everything else defaults** (defaults are the safe general behavior; restrictions are explicit; booleans take the `is` prefix):

| field | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | required | reviewer id (census attribution + packet) |
| `lens` | required | instruction markdown path (repo-authored for repo reviewers) |
| `roleLine` | derived: `Specialized Code Reviewer — <name>` | persona line placed first in the prompt |
| `mayRaise` | ALL tiers, 🚨 included — **no limits** (even a translator catching "wink → wank" in user-facing text is a real blocker) | tiers the spec allows; the citation discipline rides the base contract every reviewer gets, so 🚨 claims stay evidence-bound regardless of lens |
| `filterWeight` | `"normal"` (`low`/`normal`/`high`) | `high` = the filter leg may not silently drop this reviewer's candidates — demote/drop needs a stated reason and surfaces in the packet |
| `isFiltered` | `true` | `false` = candidates bypass the filter leg |
| `rounds` | `["all"]` | array of flags: `["first"]` / `["hunks"]` / `["first","hunks"]` / `["all"]` — see §6 |
| `triggerPaths` | `[]` | substrings gating `hunks` re-runs; **security ships `[]` — no path limitation** |
| `options` | `{}` | opaque per-reviewer pass-through (security: `referencePack`; legal: `docsSources`, `isQuestionsOnlyWithoutDocs`) — the lens owns interpretation |
| `model` | `null` | factory default |
| `isEnabled` | `true` | `false` = disabled, stated in the review summary every round |

Minimal valid file: `{"name": "a11y", "lens": ".dmtools/review/a11y.md"}` — there is no "minimal mode": every skill file defines a FULL reviewer; minimal describes authoring effort only.

## 3. Pool config — reviewPolicy schema extension

`validatePolicyShape` known keys gain `reviewers` + `promptAppend` + `required` (strictness preserved — unknown keys still throw):

```js
reviewPolicy: {
  required: ['base', 'security'],   // MERGE GATE policy: these reviewers' PASS markers
                                    // must exist on the current head before merge.
                                    // Factory default; repo owns the list ([] = gate nothing)
  reviewers: {                      // tuning/enablement; absence = factory defaults
    security: { isEnabled: true },  // factory default anyway; explicit allowed
    legal:    { isEnabled: true }   // repo-defined reviewer (skill file below)
  },
  promptAppend: {                   // ADDITIVE ONLY — appends after the lens
    base:     ['.dmtools/review/base.append.md'],
    security: ['.dmtools/review/security.append.md']
  }
}
```

Factory ships base + security enabled by default. Everything else is repo configuration — including which reviewers gate the merge (`reviewPolicy.required`).

## 4. Execution — parallel candidates, ONE verdict

Each enabled reviewer = one independent leg run over the same diff (round gating per `rounds`/`triggerPaths`). Legs write candidate files (structured findings, reviewer-attributed); **legs never post to the PR**. The merge step (§5) reads all candidate files → one census → gh-1351 recompute → ONE PR review.

- Specialist leg failure: fail-open for non-required reviewers (round proceeds, packet notes "X unavailable this round"); for `reviewPolicy.required` reviewers see §7.
- Re-firing after a failed attempt is duplicate-safe: failed legs leave no candidates (candidates are leg output files; nothing is posted until the census merge).

## 5. Filter leg = merge point (build with #1403)

The #1403 filter runs after ALL reviewer legs: input = every candidate + the diff + interaction neighborhood; output per candidate `keep | demote(<tier>) | drop` + reason. Pool-specific duties:
- **cross-reviewer dedup** (base and security flag the same injection → one identity, severity may only escalate);
- **weighted retention**: `filterWeight: high` candidates cannot be silently dropped — demote/drop requires a stated reason, surfaced in the packet;
- dropped candidates stay visible as digest lines (drop-rate ≈ 100% = misconfiguration, not quality).

Census is recomputed AFTER filtering. Density cap (gh-1351) applies to the merged census.

## 6. `rounds` semantics

- `["first"]` — initial review only. **`first` counts COMPLETED passes, not attempts**: a 429-failed leg re-fires next round until the reviewer's completion marker exists (marker = same `dmtools:` head-carried family; failed legs leave no candidates, so re-fire is duplicate-free). Budget-bounded → owner escalation.
- `["hunks"]` — only when new hunks touch `triggerPaths`. "New" = `git diff <lastReviewedHead>...HEAD` (head from the verdict/registry markers; unknown head → fail-open to full pass), materialized as `pr_new_hunks.txt` (changed files + hunk line ranges). The specialist input = `pr_new_hunks.txt` + full file contents + the frozen-code rule ("judge only the new hunks + interaction neighborhood; unchanged code is frozen unless the new hunks make it worse"). Enforcement mechanical: an inline finding must anchor inside the new hunks — otherwise advisory digest. `triggerPaths` matches the new hunks' file paths only.
- `["first","hunks"]` — both; **specialist default** (full pass up front so everything is highlighted once; near-merge re-verification without a late-surprise fresh review).
- `["all"]` — every round unconditionally.

## 7. `reviewPolicy.required` — the merge gate (the 429 scenario)

Base review succeeds, security fails on provider 429s → without a gate the PR merges with no security review. Fail-open is right for AVAILABILITY, wrong for MERGE GATING — the split lives in ONE pool-policy key, not smeared across skill files. Mechanics:
- `reviewPolicy.required` (default `['base', 'security']`) names the reviewers whose completion gates the merge; a repo may shrink it (`required: []` gates nothing) — merge rules are repo rules;
- every reviewer leg stamps a head-carried PASS marker on completion (same `dmtools:` family; old-head passes don't count after a push); the PASS marker doubles as the `first`-rounds completion counter, so it exists for EVERY reviewer regardless of this policy;
- the SM merge-time check (gh-1370 lane) gains a clause: every `reviewPolicy.required` reviewer must have a PASS marker on the CURRENT head, else merge is withheld (like red CI);
- failed required leg: retry with backoff → budget exhausted → owner escalation (never silent merge, never silent approval).

## 8. Validation — free, deterministic script (NOT agent analysis)

Ship `validate-review-skills.js` (zero-dep node, fs+JSON only) so repos can self-check and CI can gate. A WORKING example ships in the example repo (§9) — the implementation may differ, but it MUST verify at minimum:
1. skill JSON parses; `name`+`lens` present; unknown top-level fields warned (typo protection — `options` is the pass-through bucket);
2. `mayRaise` ⊆ tiers; `rounds` flags valid; `["all"]` not combined; booleans are booleans (`is` prefix);
3. lens file exists + non-empty; if the spec EXPLICITLY declares `BLOCKING` and the lens lacks the citation hint → warning;
4. duplicate reviewer names → error;
5. same-name factory-reviewer files contain only tunable fields → else error;
6. `promptAppend` targets resolve to real reviewers and files exist;
7. `reviewPolicy.reviewers.*.isEnabled` entries resolve to defined reviewers;
8. `reviewPolicy.required` entries resolve to defined reviewers (a name that resolves to nothing is a hard error — a misspelled gate silently gates nothing).
Exit codes `✅ 0 / ❌ 1` — wire next to the docs-coverage gate. The script proves the configuration is well-formed and loadable; whether a lens is any GOOD is the filter leg's job (agent work — never script work).

## 9. Worked example (live repo)

Branch [`example/reviewer-pool`](https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_worflow_test_example/tree/example/reviewer-pool) of the factory test repo — file for file:
- `.dmtools/review/legal.json` — repo-defined legal reviewer (spec, minimal-plus form)
- `.dmtools/review/legal.lens.md` — consent/privacy/terms lens with the citation discipline
- `.dmtools/review/security.append.md`, `base.append.md` — repo appends (extend-not-replace)
- `.dmtools/review/validate-review-skills.js` — the validation script EXAMPLE (implementations may differ; the §8 check list is the contract)
- `.dmtools/review/README.md` — the format contract, defaults table, worked rounds example
- `.dmtools/config.js` — the FUTURE `reviewPolicy` shape. **Do not merge this branch before this issue ships**: the current `validatePolicyShape` rejects unknown keys, so the example config fails the review leg on today's code (that is expected and is why the schema extension in §3 is part of this issue).

## 10. Rollout (checklist)

- [ ] File split: `instructions/pr_review/base|generalist|security`, both review legs point at the base set, freshness gate on (no behavior change)
- [ ] Skill-file schema + pool resolution (factory + repo dirs, same-name tuning rules, defaults §2)
- [ ] `reviewPolicy` known keys += `reviewers`, `promptAppend`, `required` (strictness preserved)
- [ ] Security reviewer skill file (explicit: `mayRaise` incl. BLOCKING, `rounds: ["first","hunks"]`, `triggerPaths: []`) + base role-line rename
- [ ] Parallel execution + candidate files + census merge; fail-open semantics for non-required reviewers
- [ ] Requires #1403: filter leg as merge point (cross-reviewer dedup, weighted retention, drop visibility)
- [ ] `reviewPolicy.required` merge gate in the gh-1370 lane (PASS markers, retry→escalate)
- [ ] Validator script + docs + worked example link

## Out of scope (by decision)
- Legal reviewer as a factory default — repo configuration (worked example above)
- Majority voting, lessons/feedback loop, polish-lap changes — separate issues after the pool + #1403 land
